rationale: Repair of trial-b04d1d014e's measured failure, keeping its validated mechanism while removing its measured cost. What the previous feedback establishes: the joint functional candidate at the two c10d::allreduce_ sites breached step_ms (256.978 ms vs 138.660 ms limit, decision no_valid_parameter_candidate) even though its mechanism worked - the separately collected objective runs measured communication_kernel_sum_ms at median max-rank 63.542 ms (rank samples 60.328/62.080/66.191 and 65.644/63.472/63.542) versus the 74.676 ms baseline, with every quality check passing (continuous checks max_abs_error 0.0, bit-exact gradient replicas). The binding_cost collector on that revision isolates the breach cause: the parent arm ran 139.58/139.86 ms while the binding-only passthrough (candidate computation omitted, the two functional sites retained) ran 253.08/231.30 ms, i.e. ~92-113 ms of pure binding cost; python_runtime pstats attribute it to the legacy global __torch_dispatch__ path (7563 intercepted ops per step, ~29 ms self plus ~12 ms torch._ops __str__, ~7 ms find_torch_dispatch_rule, ~9.4 ms dict.get), which destroyed the host/device overlap this co-saturated eager step depends on. The alignment barrier itself cost only ~+4 ms (screened 257 ms vs 253 ms passthrough). How this changes the attempt: with binding_backend frozen at legacy (binding-contract.md: unscoped functional sites take the global dispatch path over every operator; module/project replacements use direct callable boundaries unless they also install functional sites), the repair must keep the mechanism and eliminate functional dispatch entirely. The 13 allreduce_ dispatches (12x 7,087,872-element buckets closed by the 39,385,344-element embedding bucket, execution_timeline seq 21-33, stream 17 RING_LL) are issued by DDP's C++ reducer during the final backward with the project invoke 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 (target project.invoke, kind project, phase run, no parents, both ranks, 1 invocation per step) as their only call parent, so no module boundary contains them; that single project call is the one coherent editable boundary and is installed as a direct callable with zero functional sites and therefore zero global dispatch overhead. The candidate replaces exactly that call with a faithful re-execution of adapter.run - same optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) inside the timed step, same no_sync accumulation loop over state['inputs'] with the identical isinstance(model, DDP) guard, same per-microbatch loss scaling by len(inputs), same phase markers microbatch_forward/backward/synchronized_backward/optimizer_step via the same kernel_optimizer.project.discovery.phase import the adapter uses, same SGD step and end-of-step torch.cuda.synchronize, same {'loss', 'microbatch_losses'} return structure, recomputed from live state on every invocation with no caching - plus one addition: a single gloo barrier on the adapter's existing state['control'] group (the same group and API adapter.before_run already uses each invocation) issued from the main thread immediately before the final microbatch's loss.backward(), the last safe host point before the collective burst, with the autograd engine idle - unlike the previous candidate's engine-thread placement inside the c10d op. Measured justification that the targeted term is reducible: the current execution_timeline shows the leading rank submitting the burst 6.25-7.29 ms (clock-alignment bounds) before the peer, its first NCCL kernel running 9.702 ms against the 3.275-3.675 ms peer/floor, hooked rank sums 64.07/70.56 ms against the 74.676 ms clean baseline max-rank, and the collective_calibration floor at exactly these sizes/dtypes is 12x3.593 + 19.642 = ~62.8 ms per rank. The barrier emits no NCCL kernel and touches no tensors, so bytes, DDP flags, bucket layout, algorithm, transport, op order and arithmetic are untouched and losses, gradients (including the bit-exact cross-rank replica property of NCCL allreduce) and post-update parameters are unchanged; verification done before submission: on CPU the replacement is bit-identical to the real adapter.run (loss, microbatch_losses, every gradient, every post-update parameter) and a real two-rank gloo DDP run shows one barrier per step, no hang, and bit-exact gradient replicas. Route labels distinguish setup failure (setup_no_control_group_parent_step, unsupported_state_parent_run, build-time missing-parent raise), runtime failure (barrier_failed_<Exc>) and the permanently disabled fallback (alignment_disabled_parent_step), each of which serves exact parent semantics. Hypothesis to be tested by the framework, not assumed: aligning the hosts immediately before the synchronized backward removes the pre-burst component of the submission offset, so the leading rank's first bucket kernel falls from ~9.7 ms toward the ~3.3-3.6 ms floor and communication_kernel_sum_ms drops from 74.676 ms toward ~63-67 ms, consistent with the 63.5 ms already measured for burst-start alignment and the ~62.8 ms synchronized floor; step_ms stays under the 138.660 ms limit (expected ~132-134 ms) because the replacement adds no dispatch layer, the barrier's clean cost is sub-ms, and the leading rank's bounded host wait replaces device spin its kernels previously absorbed while the trailing rank - which paces the 132.06 ms baseline max-rank wall - passes the barrier without waiting. Explicit unknowns the framework's measurement must decide: (a) the clean-run skew magnitude (all timeline numbers are hook-perturbed; only the ~+4 ms binding_cost delta estimates the step_ms exposure cleanly); (b) residual skew re-developed between barrier exit and the first bucket dispatch, and across the burst, bounding the gain short of the floor; (c) the gloo barrier's own unprofiled latency on this control group; (d) the objective's 64-80 ms run-to-run spread means acceptance rests on the median-of-3 protocol, not any single value; (e) if the control group is missing, the state shape is unexpected, or the barrier raises, the replacement falls back to exact parent step semantics so correctness, replicas and the negative control are unaffected - the barrier touches no tensors, so numerics are invariant by construction. The earlier execution_plan CUDA-graph attempt (trial-df7761708a) is not revived: no capture, no snapshots, no side streams, no per-op re-dispatch, no additional CUDA allocations, so its capture failure and allocator-inflation failure class cannot recur.
setup_work: build(context) is pure host-side binding: it reads context['references']['5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0'] (the current adapter.run) as the fallback parent, reads state['control'] and state['distributed'] from the already-prepared adapter state, binds context.get('record_route', no-op) and resets module-level counters; it raises a concise setup failure (project_alignment_replacement_missing_parent_reference) if the parent reference is absent. No GPU work, no CUDA allocations, no parameter transformations, no snapshots, no CUDA graphs, no retained pools, no new process groups (the barrier reuses the adapter's existing state['control'] gloo group), no fixture-dependent caching. Expected installation cost is a few milliseconds of Python, comparable to the 4.1-6.8 ms setup receipts of the previous revision. Memory scope: setup allocation is zero beyond module-level Python scalars; during execution the replacement performs exactly the allocations adapter.run already performs (per-microbatch activations and the torch.stack of detached losses), so peak_allocated_bytes, peak_reserved_bytes and the lifecycle peaks are unchanged from baseline - no counter decrease is claimed and none should be expected; outputs and gradients are recomputed from live state on every invocation.
quality_risks: Numerics: the replacement executes the same operator sequence as adapter.run with the same tensors, order and scaling; the only addition is a gloo barrier that touches no tensors. CPU verification is bit-identical against the real adapter.run (loss, microbatch_losses, all gradients, all post-update parameters) and a real two-rank gloo DDP run reproduces bit-exact gradient replicas, but the GPU run could still expose an unexpected interaction; in that case quality comparisons (grad_atol/grad_rtol, parameter_atol/parameter_rtol, exact replica check, negative control) would fail loudly rather than silently pass.

step_ms constraint (<= 138.660 ms): the trailing rank passes the barrier without waiting and keeps pacing the max-rank wall (~132.06 ms baseline); the leading rank's host wait replaces device spin its first kernel previously absorbed; added exposure is the barrier's own latency (sub-ms expected, never measured unprofiled on this group) plus the Python re-execution of the accumulation loop, which mirrors adapter.run's own Python overhead with no dispatch layer. Headroom is ~6.6 ms; the unknown clean-run skew magnitude and run-to-run step variance could consume it, and only the framework's paired measurement decides.

Barrier asymmetry/hang: the barrier decision path is deterministic and identical on both ranks (same state keys, same code, symmetric collective counts from DDP), so one rank cannot reach the barrier while the peer skips it except in an already-fatal divergence; the wait is bounded by the control group's 120 s timeout against the 900 s worker timeout. A barrier exception permanently disables alignment on that rank and serves exact parent step semantics afterwards; cross-rank barrier count divergence after such a failure is bounded by the same timeout and would surface as a loud failure, not wrong numbers.

Placement inside the timed region: the barrier runs inside the step (inside the synchronized_backward phase marker, immediately before the final loss.backward()) and is sequential with the evaluator's before_run barrier on the same process group - both ranks execute the same number of barrier calls per iteration cycle, so gloo FIFO matching holds and no collective is starved; the torch_communication diagnostic invocations execute the same path and the barrier emits no NCCL kernel, so the collector still observes the same 13 kernels with the same payloads.

Coverage: the single declared replacement call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 is invoked exactly once per invocation on each rank; no inner calls are eliminated - all 13 allreduce_ dispatches, all module forwards/backwards and the optimizer step still execute through the original DDP/autograd machinery inside the replacement, so consumers remain valid by construction; route labels (aligned_final_backward_barrier, setup_no_control_group_parent_step, unsupported_state_parent_run, barrier_failed_<Exc>, alignment_disabled_parent_step) are diagnostic self-report only, never a substitute for the framework's output checks, runtime coverage or trace evidence.

Objective risk: if the clean-run cross-rank skew is materially smaller than the hook-perturbed 6.25-7.29 ms bounds, or residual skew re-develops quickly between barrier exit and the first bucket dispatch, the median objective gain may shrink toward zero while the barrier cost remains; acceptance then fails on improvement rather than on correctness. No missing measurement or unknown transport capability is treated as an observed fact anywhere in this proposal.
